title: Run-Length Encoding
description:
# Run-Length Encoding

Run-length encoding compresses a string by replacing each *run* of one or more identical consecutive characters with that character followed by the length of the run.

For example, `aaabbc` becomes `a3b2c1`.

## Input

A single line of text (no spaces).

## Output

The run-length encoding of the string.

```
Input:
aaabbc

Output:
a3b2c1
```

## Think about

- Walk through the string and group consecutive equal characters.
- Every run, even of length 1, is written with its count (`abc → a1b1c1`).
starterCode:
s = input()

# TODO: print the run-length encoding of s (e.g. aaabbc -> a3b2c1)
hints: Walk through the string grouping consecutive equal characters.
Track the current run's character and length; when the next char differs, emit `char + count` and start a new run. Don't forget the final run.

```
i = 0;  result = ""
while i < length(s)
    j = i
    while j < length(s) and s[j] = s[i]
        j = j + 1
    result = result + s[i] + (j - i)
    i = j
print result
```
